source: MAFF Department of Agricultural Extension (នាយកដ្ឋានផ្សព្វផ្សាយកសិកម្ម) - "ដំណាំក្រូចពោធិសាត់" (Pursat Orange Cultivation Guide), 2016, 26pp
text:
Pursat orange fruit is harvested once it reaches full size for its variety; because the fruit often stays greenish even when ripe, farmers judge readiness mainly by fruit size and by counting the weeks or months since flowering (the source notes roughly 8 months from flowering to harvest) rather than by skin color change alone.

Fruit should be cut from the tree with pruning shears or a knife, leaving a short piece of stem attached, rather than pulled by hand, to avoid tearing the peel or damaging the branch. After harvest, fruit is sorted and graded by size before being sold, since larger, unblemished fruit commands a better price in the market.
